Text: Annotations are declared in Java using the {{c1::@interface}} keyword.
Extra: They implicitly extend the java.lang.annotation.Annotation interface.

Text: By default, custom annotations are stored with a retention policy of {{c1::RetentionPolicy.CLASS}}.
Extra: This means they are recorded in the .class file but not loaded by the JVM at runtime, making them invisible to reflection checks.

Text: To make an annotation accessible via Java Reflection at runtime, you must annotate it with {{c1::@Retention(RetentionPolicy.RUNTIME)}}.
Extra: This is required for runtime configuration frameworks (e.g. Spring, Jackson).

Text: The {{c1::@Target}} meta-annotation defines which program elements (methods, fields, types, etc.) the custom annotation can be applied to.
Extra: If @Target is omitted, the annotation can be applied to any declaration context (but not type use contexts).

Text: The meta-annotation {{c1::@Inherited}} allows subclasses to inherit class-level annotations from their superclass.
Extra: Note that @Inherited does NOT work on interfaces or methods; only superclass annotations are inherited.

Text: The {{c1::@Override}} annotation instructs the compiler to verify that the method signature matches a method from a superclass or interface.
Extra: This prevents signature mismatch bugs. It causes a compiler error if the parent method is private, static, or if the parameter types differ.

Text: Using a deprecated element triggers a compiler warning, but if it is marked with {{c1::forRemoval = true}}, the compiler triggers a terminal deprecation warning.
Extra: Example: @Deprecated(since = "9", forRemoval = true). This alerts developers that the API will be deleted in a future version.

Text: The {{c1::@SuppressWarnings}} annotation accepts a String array containing warning types (e.g. "deprecation", "unchecked") to ignore.
Extra: It suppresses warnings for the annotated element and all nested declarations.

Text: An interface marked with {{c1::@FunctionalInterface}} must have exactly {{c2::one}} abstract method.
Extra: Default methods, static methods, and public methods overriding Object methods do not count against this limit.

Text: To prevent heap pollution warnings on generic varargs methods, developers can use the {{c1::@SafeVarargs}} annotation.
Extra: This is only legal on static, final, or private methods. The programmer promises that the method only reads from the varargs array.

Text: To allow multiple instances of the same annotation on a single element, the annotation type must be marked with {{c1::@Repeatable}}.
Extra: @Repeatable requires specifying a container annotation type which holds an array of the repeatable annotation.

Text: The meta-annotation {{c1::@Documented}} ensures the custom annotation is visible in the generated Javadoc.
Extra: By default, annotations are omitted from Javadoc. @Documented ensures API clients see the annotations applied to classes or methods.

Text: Annotation elements are restricted to primitives, String, Class, enums, annotations, or {{c1::one-dimensional arrays}} of these.
Extra: Wrapper objects (like Integer) and multi-dimensional arrays (like String[][]) are illegal element types.

Text: If multiple repeatable annotations are present on an element, calling reflection's getAnnotation() for that type returns {{c1::null}}.
Extra: This happens because the compiler wraps them in a container annotation. You must query the container class or use getAnnotationsByType() instead.

Text: The reflection interface {{c1::AnnotatedElement}} is implemented by Class, Method, and Field, providing methods like isAnnotationPresent().
Extra: This allows runtime engines to dynamically inspect annotations and configure behavior accordingly.

Text: In reflection, calling {{c1::getDeclaredAnnotations()}} returns only annotations directly declared on the element, ignoring inherited ones.
Extra: In contrast, getAnnotations() returns all annotations present on the element, including inherited ones.

Text: Under the hood, runtime annotations returned by reflection are implemented as JVM-synthesized {{c1::dynamic proxy classes}}.
Extra: These classes delegate element accessors to an AnnotationInvocationHandler mapping to constant-pool metadata.

Text: If `@Target` is omitted, the custom annotation can be applied to {{c1::any declaration context}}.
Extra: This includes classes, methods, fields, parameters, constructors, local variables, etc., but excludes TYPE_USE contexts.
